facts.fact: The document's own caption records President Buhari 'unveiling' the National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy on 28 November 2019 and its contents list his speech 'launching' it; the President's mandate page says it was 'developed in line with the Presidential directives' and the Minister signs the foreword as a 'National document'. No gazette or Federal Executive Council act is named.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030

facts.fact: The text is held on the NITDA site and is titled for 2020-2030; the pillars, objectives and a 95% digital-literacy target 'within the next 10 years' are stated in it. The as-of is the document's own date.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030

facts.fact: The strategy sets eight pillars with listed government actions and dated targets, among them 70% broadband penetration in four years and 95% digital literacy in ten; it states no cost or budget for them.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030

facts.fact: The foreword says the Federal Ministry of Communications and Digital Economy was assigned, among its priorities, the development and implementation of the strategy; the President directed the Minister to work with all relevant agencies, and the strategy proposes a National Digital Economy Council not yet shown as established.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030

facts.fact: The document ties no budget line or allocation to the strategy; it says only that government will 'provide funding' for some actions, such as networking federal public institutions, with no amount or source.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030

facts.fact: The President's mandate page says he is 'happy with its level of implementation so far'; no report against the strategy's targets is given. The page is undated, so the document's published date is used.
facts.system: National Digital Economy Policy and Strategy 2020-2030
